items.statement: Computed solution structure and equivalence or inequivalence of para environments
items.expected: Establish a physically valid, singly threaded rotaxane model through actual calculations and explain whether its macrocycle/axle organization gives equivalent or inequivalent para environments in the modeled solvent and states. The source hydrogen-bond-organized asymmetric pose, with one ring more parallel-displaced against the CF3 axle aryl ring and the other more tilted/offset, is a sufficient reference account; no particular contact checklist or asymmetric outcome is mandatory. A fully supported equivalent environment or alternative organization passes directly. Distinguish equivalence within one computed conformation from equivalence after averaging symmetry-related conformations; an ensemble claim requires justified state mapping and weights or applicable physical symmetry, and does not establish identical local geometries. A demonstrated symmetry operation on an actually computed pose may establish a related pose without a second independent quantum calculation, but does not establish solution populations or exchange rates. A bare symmetry assumption, crystal distance, unthreaded mixture or generic contact list without a valid computed solution model fails.

items.statement: Computed para-site response and its implication for electrophilic amination
items.expected: Report actual numerical para-site electronic responses with consistent physical definitions and mapping, comparing the two sites within the same computed conformation or within an explicitly justified ensemble. Infer whether those results support different or equivalent susceptibility under that model. In the reference asymmetric pose, the axle-stacked ring para carbon is more electron rich: source NPA −0.277 versus −0.259 e is context without a hard window. A physically substantiated alternative response comparison, including established equivalence, passes directly; the reference charge sign is not mandatory for another valid descriptor or conformation. An ensemble average must use justified state mapping and weights or demonstrated applicable symmetry on computed states, and must be distinguished from each local site response. Mere symmetry assumptions or arbitrary averaging do not replace the numerical calculations. Explain the relevance to amination without equating a descriptor with a barrier, rate ratio or unique reactive site. Mirror relabeling alone is not a physical reversal; experimental product preference is not computed electronic evidence.

items.statement: What the computed substrate structure and site responses establish about net enantioselectivity
items.expected: Use the actual computed substrate structure, numerical site responses and demonstrated relevant symmetry relationships to assess the explanatory reach for the given enantioselectivity and mono/di-amination time trend. Either supported local inequivalence or established equivalence can answer this item. Distinguish a conditional substrate-site preference from selection of net enantiomeric excess: substrate-only structure and responses do not determine chiral catalyst selection or the required reaction kinetics. A symmetry relation may be established by an explicit operation on an actually computed pose without an additional independent quantum calculation; it does not establish ensemble populations or exchange rates. Relate the resulting inference to the observations without claiming a calculated kinetic-resolution rate or quantitative ee. The source permits a less-hindered-ring alternative, so neither an electronic descriptor nor an equivalence result proves a unique catalytic mechanism. A generic limitations paragraph or assumed symmetry without the actual structural/site argument fails. No catalyst calculation, transition state or ensemble calculation is newly required.
